topic: Function transformation: horizontal and vertical shifts
problem: The function f is defined by f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7. The graph of y = g(x) is the result of shifting the graph of y = f(x) right 3 units and down 2 units. Which of the following defines g?

bad.why: Rewriting f and all four choices in vertex form by hand to compare vertices is repeated algebra the overlapping graphs make unnecessary.
Not a modeling question: the shift must actually be applied to f, and translating 'right 3' as x+3 is the classic sign trap.

algebraFirst.description: Substitutes x-3 into f and subtracts 2, expanding (x-3)^2-4(x-3)+7-2 by hand to x^2-10x+26, then matches the choice.

explanationNotes: Shifting right 3 replaces x with x-3 (the sign looks backwards) and shifting down 2 subtracts 2 from the output, so g(x) = f(x-3) - 2. Graphing that next to the choices shows exactly one choice lying on top of it; the vertex moving from (2, 3) to (5, 1) is a quick check of the direction. Identity regression is an equally good default: x_1 = [1...5] and f(x_1-3) - 2 ~ ax_1^2 + bx_1 + c return a = 1, b = -10, c = 26 in three rows, and it works even without answer choices.
